**Executive Order 13769**, titled **Protecting the Nation from Foreign Terrorist Entry into the United States**, labeled the "**Muslim ban**" by President Donald Trump and his supporters[1][2] and critics alike,[3][4] and commonly known as such,[5] or commonly referred to as the **Muslim travel ban**, **Trump travel ban**, the **Trump Muslim travel ban**, or the **Trump Muslim Immigration Ban**, was an executive order signed by President Trump.

Except for the extent to which it was blocked by various courts, it was in effect from January 27, 2017, until March 6, 2017, when it was superseded by Executive Order 13780, a second order sharing the same title.

In the first weeks of Trump's presidency Turkey renewed its call for safe zones and proposed a new plan for them, the Trump administration has spoken with several other Sunni Arab States regarding safe zones, and Russia has asked for clarification regarding any Trump administration plan regarding safe zones.
The UN High Commissioner on Refugees and Bashar al-Assad have dismissed safe zones as unworkable.

On January 24, 2017 the hashtag "#NoBanNoWall" first was seen on social media platform Twitter quickly after Donald Trump released news of executive order 13769.[270] The use of social media platforms such as Twitter, Facebook, and Instagram became a catalyst for an opposition movement that resulted in political mobilization and awareness of the issue.
The #nobannowall movement has been used in multiple social media platforms such as Twitter, Facebook, Tumblr, Instagram, Flickr and more.

On January 25, 2017 protesters gathered at Washington Square Park in New York and chanted: "No ban, no wall".[271] These chants were soon used in Twitter as #nobannowall to protest President Trump's border wall and Muslim ban policies.
As the hashtag became popular on Twitter it was used on other social media platforms.
There are multiple Facebook groups and pages on #nobannowall along with events that were created for protests at various locations.
There are currently 276K posts on Instagram with the hashtag #nobannowall[272] and this shows the use of various social media platforms for this social movement.
Conservative supporters of the wall and executive order responded with social media support of hashtags #BuildTheWall[273] and #BanTheMuslims,[274] among others.
